questions.question: Electric current is defined as:
options: The energy carried by a circuit
The rate of flow of charge — I = Q ÷ Δt, in coulombs per second
The number of electrons stored in a battery

questions.question: 30 C of charge passes through a bulb in 10 s. The current is:
A charger delivers 0,5 A for 2 minutes. The charge moved is:
options: 60 C — Q = I × Δt = 0,5 × 120, after converting minutes to seconds

questions.question: Conventional current is taken to flow:
options: From the positive terminal through the external circuit to the negative terminal — while electrons drift the opposite way
From negative to positive through the external circuit
In whichever direction the electrons move

subtopics.title: Potential Difference, Emf and the Volt

questions.question: Potential difference is defined as the:
options: Work done per unit charge — V = W ÷ Q, in joules per coulomb

questions.question: 24 J of work moves 8 C of charge through a resistor. The potential difference across it is:
A 12 V battery pushes 5 C of charge around a circuit. The energy transferred is:
The emf of a battery is the voltmeter reading across its terminals when:
options: No current flows — the open-circuit reading; under load the terminal pd is slightly less, because of internal resistance
The battery is connected to a motor

subtopics.title: Ammeters and Voltmeters — Reading the Circuit

questions.question: An ammeter is connected:
options: In series, so that the charge it counts actually passes through it

questions.question: An ideal ammeter has:
options: Very low resistance — so that inserting it barely changes the current it measures
No need for any connection rules

questions.question: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component because it:
options: Needs the full current through itself
Compares the energy per coulomb on the two sides of the component — and its very high resistance keeps it from stealing current
Is cheaper to wire that way

questions.question: Wiring an ammeter in parallel across a battery is dangerous because its near-zero resistance:
options: Invites a huge current through the meter — a short circuit
Blocks all current in the circuit

subtopics.title: Resistance — the Friction of the Wire

questions.question: Microscopically, resistance arises because moving electrons:
options: Repel each other out of the wire
Are too heavy to move quickly
Repeatedly collide with the vibrating ions of the metal lattice, transferring energy that appears as heat

questions.question: Doubling the length of a wire, everything else unchanged:
options: Doubles its resistance — more lattice to cross means more collisions

questions.question: Making a wire thicker:
options: Decreases its resistance — a larger cross-sectional area offers more lanes for the flow

questions.question: As a metallic conductor heats up, its resistance:
options: Increases — hotter ions vibrate more violently, so electrons collide more often

subtopics.title: The Water Pump on the Roof

questions.question: In the water-feature picture, the battery is the pump because it:
options: Gives every litre — every coulomb — a parcel of energy before sending it around

questions.question: A battery goes flat because:
options: Its chemical energy is used up — the charge itself is never consumed
All its charge has been used up
The electrons in it wear out
The current leaks out of the wires

questions.question: A 9 V battery reads 8,5 V across its terminals while driving a motor. This shows:
options: The motor has stolen 0,5 V of charge
Terminal pd under load is less than the emf — some energy is spent inside the battery itself

questions.question: In the stadium picture, current corresponds to:
options: The number of supporters inside the stadium
The number of supporters passing through the gate every second

questions.question: The current on the far side of a bulb, compared with the near side, is:
options: The same — charge is not used up; the bulb takes only the energy the charge carries
Smaller, because the bulb consumes current
Larger, because the bulb pushes it on

questions.question: In a metal wire, the particles that actually drift along are:
options: Positive ions moving from positive to negative
Electrons, drifting from negative to positive — opposite to the conventional current arrow
Protons moving from negative to positive

questions.question: The corridor picture says a wire's resistance is highest when the wire is:
Kettle elements are made of nichrome rather than copper because nichrome:
options: Resists strongly, deliberately converting electrical energy to heat
Carries current with almost no resistance

questions.question: Heating a wire raises its resistance because:
options: The wire gets longer and thinner only
The lattice ions vibrate harder, so the electrons collide with them more often
